programme: NOTCH1 sets vascular smooth-muscle/endothelial and keratinocyte differentiation state; NFKBIB (IkB-beta) gates the classic NF-kB/TNF inflammatory module in its own target set (TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL5, PTGS2, NOS2, SOD2); PIN1 reinforces NF-kB- and cyclin/MYC-driven proliferative signaling; FGF2 drives local angiogenesis; KLF10 and ASH1L run the TGF-beta/SMAD (SMAD2/3/4/7, TGFB1, TIMP1, FOXP3) arm that couples this inflammation to tissue remodeling and Treg/Th17 balance.
role_in_a: In vessel wall biology this combination underlies chronic vascular inflammation and remodeling: NOTCH1 controls smooth-muscle-cell phenotype switching and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition; NFKBIB's target genes (TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL5, NOS2, PTGS2, SOD2) are the canonical NF-kB inflammatory signature of endothelium and plaque macrophages; PIN1 amplifies NF-kB/cyclin-driven proliferation in smooth muscle and macrophages; FGF2 drives plaque neovascularization; KLF10/ASH1L shape the TGF-beta-driven fibrotic and matrix response of the vessel wall.
role_in_b: In skin the same factors plausibly run keratinocyte hyperproliferation and the dermal inflammatory-vascular response of psoriatic plaques: NOTCH1 is required for normal keratinocyte differentiation and its dysregulation is linked to epidermal hyperproliferation; NFKBIB's target module is the TNF/NF-kB signature that anti-TNF biologics target in psoriasis; PIN1 supports the hyperproliferative keratinocyte state; FGF2 drives the dermal capillary proliferation that is histologically characteristic of psoriatic plaques; KLF10/ASH1L's TGF-beta-SMAD/FOXP3 module tracks the Treg/Th17 imbalance and matrix remodeling of psoriatic dermis.
shared_axis: A TNF/NF-kB inflammatory loop overlaid on Notch- and TGF-beta-SMAD-controlled remodeling and FGF2-driven angiogenesis would produce endothelial activation, smooth-muscle proliferation and plaque neovascularization in the vessel wall, and keratinocyte hyperproliferation, dermal capillary growth and Treg/Th17 imbalance in skin — the same circuitry run in two different resident cell types, which is consistent with the clinically recognized excess cardiovascular risk seen in psoriasis patients.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target genes (NF-kB target set under NFKBIB, SMAD set under KLF10, classic Notch targets HES1/HEY1), and NOTCH1 is independently placed in cardiovascular disease by Open Targets, so this is not an arbitrary grouping. But the record itself is almost empty: no literature was retrieved for any of the 12 factors under either disease, and Open Targets records no Psoriasis association for any factor at all, so the disease-to-disease link rests on general pathway reasoning about NF-kB/TNF and Notch/TGF-beta biology rather than on anything retrieved for this specific pair.
how_to_falsify: In matched patients with both psoriasis and subclinical atherosclerosis, compare NOTCH1 and NF-kB(p65) occupancy (ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN) at TNF/IL1B/CXCL8 in lesional keratinocytes versus carotid plaque macrophages/smooth muscle cells from the same individuals, and test whether pharmacological Notch inhibition (gamma-secretase inhibitor) or NF-kB inhibition concordantly reduces keratinocyte hyperproliferation markers and vascular inflammatory markers. If target-gene activity does not co-vary across the two tissues in the same patients, or inhibition moves one tissue's phenotype without the other's, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Blood-derived (CVD) and skin-derived (psoriasis) networks are being compared computationally, not from paired tissue in the same patients, so 'concordance' here is a transcriptional-network property, not direct cross-tissue evidence. Support fractions for the carrying factors (21-24 of 64 comparisons, ~33-38%) are moderate, not near-universal, across only 4 independent cohort pairs. The single-view exclusions (FOXD1, HMBOX1, FOSB, etc.) show the story is not built on one subgroup, and the tissue-generic exclusions (FOS, JUNB, SPI1, IKZF1, KLF2/6, ETS2, RUNX2, ID2, TFE3, E2F3, CEBPG) mean the account deliberately does not reach for generic myeloid/AP-1 master regulators of blood or skin inflammation — their absence here is by design. ASXL1 (highest-recurring factor, 31/64) has its own strong Open Targets CVD association via clonal-hematopoiesis-linked targets (FABP4, CDKN2A/B) but no psoriasis link of any kind, so it was left out of the shared-programme story rather than forced in.
